paragraphs: Louma Bakery is named after my sister and a tribute to the warmth of her presence. A friend once said, “Being around Louma is like pulling fresh cookies from the oven.” She teaches us to savor the little moments. To me, her spirit has always embodied the values of a great neighborhood bakery: comfort, connection, and community.

Our West LA kitchen is rooted in European baking traditions with a Levantine twist. We serve fresh breads, classic pastries, and seasonal offerings; think organic seeded sourdough meets our house-made fattoush salad.

Alongside our commitment to artisanal baking, our mission is to create supportive training and employment opportunities for individuals with learning and developmental differences in a professional bakery setting. Grounded in Louma’s own experience, we believe that everyone deserves an opportunity to grow, contribute, and cultivate their passion. All profits from the bakery will go directly to our nonprofit parent, the Louma Initiative, a 501(c)(3) public charity that fosters meaningful opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental differences.
Dedicated to my sister and her sweet tooth, Louma Bakery is a space to meet each other where we are and share in good food.
She’s so excited to have you!

sections.title: Sister-run
paragraphs: Louma is run by sisters, each of us bringing something different to the table. We grew up in Los Angeles, and this bakery is our love letter to the city that raised us.

sections.title: Our roots, on the plate
paragraphs: Our kitchen is grounded in classic European baking, with the flavors we grew up with in a Lebanese home. Think za’atar croissants, labneh, kaak breads, orange-blossom brioche buns, and rose water infused drinks.
Some recipes come straight from our family kitchen. Our granola is my older sister’s recipe: toasted nuts, seeds, and oats with honey and maple syrup, our favorite healthy snack to have at home.

sections.title: Ingredients we care about
paragraphs: We source our za’atar, orange-blossom water, rose water, and pomegranate molasses from Lebanon, because those flavors should taste the way we remember them. Our butter and pastry flour are imported from France by partners we trust, our olive oil is Greek, and our organic bread flour and rye seeds come from Utah. Our matcha and hojicha powders come directly from Japan, and our coffee is roasted here in Los Angeles by our neighbors at Goodboybob.

sections.title: Stay a while
paragraphs: We don’t think a sense of belonging can be manufactured. It grows slowly through small, everyday moments: neighbors saying good morning, friends gathering to catch up and enjoy a special treat, and familiar faces becoming part of the rhythm of the bakery. Louma is here most days welcoming people in, and she’s so excited to have you.
